Sports.title: Vincent Kompany taken to hospital as air ambulance lands at Bayern Munich training ground
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany taken to hospital as air ambulance lands at Bayern Munich training ground

Vincent Kompany has been rushed to hospital, with an air ambulance landing at the Bayern Munich training ground on Säbener Straße on Friday

View 2 Images Vincent Kompany has been taken to hospital (Image: 2026 FC Bayern)

Vincent Kompany has been taken to hospital, with an air ambulance spotted landing at Bayern Munich's training ground on Friday. It comes as the head coach of the Bavarians has been battling a viral infection.

While the 40-year-old was able to take the reins of Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig on Saturday, BILD claim that Kompany had to lie down on a sofa in his coach's room at half-time and after the win. Further concerns sparked when assistant coach, Aaron Danks, took his place for the Bundesliga titans' pre-match press conference on Tuesday, looking to their Champions League clash with Arsenal.

It is reported that Kompany underwent a thorough examination by medical experts, including team doctor, Prof. Roland Schmidt, missing training sessions on Monday and Tuesday. Danks said of Kompany during the press conference: "The most important thing we are encouraging him to do right now is to rest and take the time he needs – however long that may take."

To the surprise of many, Kompany took charge of his side for Wednesday's clash under the bright lights of the Allianz Arena. Speaking after the 2-2 draw, the Belgian told the press: "As a coach, you always want to do everything and accomplish everything.

"I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn't listen to my body, and then at some point my body said: 'Stop now.'"

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Bayern confirmed in a statement that the manager had been taken to hospital: "Vincent Kompany had to receive medical attention on Friday after collapsing during a training session involving FC Bayern Amateure. The first-team head coach had been watching the reserve team's training session. Kompany is undergoing thorough examinations in hospital and will remain under medical supervision. Until further notice, his coaching staff will oversee training sessions and matches."

It has been a tough week all round at Säbener Straße, with a number of first-team players missing Wednesday's Champions League clash.

Not only was Michael Olise forced out of the match as a result of a one-match suspension for picking up two yellow cards in quick succession against Viking last week, but Jamal Musiala also missed out as he continues to recover from a thigh injury sustained during the late September international break.

View 2 Images Aaron Danks took Bayern Munich's pre-match press conference (Image: 2026 FC Bayern)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bayern captain, Joshua Kimmich, also missed the match as a result of a death within his immediate family. A statement from the Bavarians read: "Due to a death in his immediate family, Joshua Kimmich is not in the squad today for the match against Arsenal London.

"On behalf of the family, we ask that his privacy and grief be respected, and that further inquiries and reporting be refrained from. In deep sympathy, the entire FC Bayern stands by Joshua Kimmich's side."

Sports.title: Bukayo Saka delivers Arsenal huge injury blow as extent of thigh issue revealed
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka delivers Arsenal huge injury blow as extent of thigh issue revealed

Arsenal star Bukayo Saka could be out until December with a thigh injury sustained in Wednesday night's Champions League draw at Bayern Munich

View 2 Images Saka is set to be out until December (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Bukayo Saka has delivered Arsenal a huge blow and could be out until December with a thigh injury sustained in the Gunners' draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday night.

‌



‌



Saka is undergoing further scans on the injury which will determine the exact lay-off but Arsenal are already resigned to Saka being out for several weeks.

‌



The England star will also miss the Three Lions' Nations League fixtures next month including the group decider in Spain on November 15 after another massive setback.

‌



Incredibly, this is Saka’s 11th injury since September 2024 and is a huge blow for Arsenal’s title defence and Champions League games as he will be sweating on being ready to face Real Madrid at the Emirates on December 9.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He will definitely miss the Gunners' trip to Anfield on November 1. Manchester City travel to the Emirates on November 29 and it's the north London derby at Tottenham a week later.

Arteta said: “When a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, he's restricted to movement, they are not good signs.

‌



“He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury. We will know more probably tomorrow."

Arteta insisted he does not fear that Saka is suffering from burnout but admits that he has become a “different” player and he may be in danger of losing some of his robustness.

‌



View 2 Images Saka will miss England's Nations League fixtures in November (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Arteta said: “Well, it's certainly been different in the last year or so. Obviously the demands that we are putting to every player are immense.

‌



“The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

“So look at us now, we have to play on Sunday afternoon, then we have to go away, we have to play on Wednesday evening, then we have to play on Saturday. So you go less than 66, 67 hours between games.

‌



“On top of everything that we are putting, every hour is important. If they can support all the demands that we are putting to the players in that sense, that would be as well really appreciated from everybody.

“And I'm saying for every team as well, because we know what we are demanding from those players."

Sports.title: Man Utd manager candidate reminded of 'big blows' as ex-boss criticises previous record
Sports.content:
Man Utd manager candidate reminded of 'big blows' as ex-boss criticises previous record

Julian Nagelsmann has been warned against taking the Manchester United job by Oliver Kahn, who cited the lack of managerial continuity at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Julian Nagelsmann has been linked with Manchester United (Image: Joosep Martinson - FIFA, FIFA via Getty Images)

Germany legend Oliver Kahn has told Julian Nagelsmann to avoid the Manchester United job - and has commented on his recent exploits, which have somewhat underwhelmed.

‌



‌



He is understood to be one of the favourites to takeover from Michael Carrick. The current Red Devils manager will be in charge for this weekend's clash against Bournemouth, but that has not stopped the rumours about potential candidates from appearing. Nagelsmann and Aston Villa manager Unai Emery are believed to be the two favourites for the United position.

‌



The former is a free agent having left his position as manager of Germany after they were knocked out of the World Cup round of 32 by Paraguay in shocking fashion. But as the links continue to appear, Kahn believes Nagelsmann should think twice before moving to Old Trafford.

‌



He said: "From his point of view, it's not an easy situation. He isn't someone with a great deal of experience, particularly when it comes to foreign teams."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



On the RTL/Sky Germany show Triple - der Hagedorn Fußballtalk, Kahn added: "The Premier League and Manchester United have not been known for much continuity in the managerial position in recent years.

"He has to ask himself, 'What is my next step? Does it have to be the right one? Or do I immediately associate it with an enormous risk like Manchester United, where essentially every manager in recent years has failed sooner or later?'

‌



"You should look very carefully at where you're going. Bayern Munich and the national team were already big blows for him. You have to think carefully, 'Where do my strengths lie? Which club can I really help?' I think Julian is someone who can develop a club and a team and take them further. Whether Manchester United are the right next step for that is something only he can know."

View 2 Images Kahn warned Nagelsmann about United (Image: Alex Grimm, Getty Images)

‌



Nagelsmann was always tipped to eventually lead a major outfit, and he was given the Bayern job in 2021. He claimed the Bundesliga title in his first season, but has knocked out of the German Cup in the second round, losing 5-0 to Borussia Monchengladbach.

They were also shocked in the Champions League, losing on aggregate to Villarreal who scored their crucial goal in the 88th minute at the Allianz Arena. He failed to see out his second year, being axed in late March with Bayern choosing to appoint Thomas Tuchel.

Nagelsmann did land the Germany job in 2023 but underwhelmed in two major tournaments. They were knocked out of a home Euros in the last eight by winners Spain. This summer their World Cup hopes ended at the hands of Paraguay in the Round of 32, who beat them on penalties.

Sports.title: 'Like a mini World Cup' - Jacks sees positives in England's tri-series troubles
Sports.content:
Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory.

England had looked set to bounce back from an 87-run hammering by Pakistan as Harry Brook's record-breaking 202 saw Sri Lanka set a massive 430 to win their match on Thursday, only for them to pull off a remarkable run chase on the penultimate ball.

The two-wicket defeat means England arrive in Lahore knowing they must beat both Pakistan on Sunday and then Sri Lanka on Thursday to give themselves a chance of of reaching the final on Saturday, October 31.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Mark Butcher describe Harry Brook as 'box office' after his record ODI innings against Sri Lanka.

Jacks pointed out that England were faced with a similar predicament en route to winning the 2019 World Cup and, looking ahead to 2027 edition in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, he views this next week as important preparation.

"It's my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup-style pressure." Jacks told the Press Association on Friday. "You can't replicate that in training or a bilateral series.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook reacts to his record-breaking double century in England's defeat to Sri Lanka, but insists the milestone means little after ending up on the losing side.

"In World Cups you have to bounce back, I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two [against India and New Zealand] and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward [into the semi-finals].

"I'm not saying it's the same thing but it's a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures.

"Every game that we play is a stepping stone towards South Africa in 12 months' time. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins. There's always going to be bumps."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from England against Sri Lanka during their ODI tri-series game.

Jacks was part of a six-strong bowling group that was pummelled to all parts by Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

Sam Curran, in his second match back after groin surgery, was the most experienced of the attack but ended up being the most expensive, conceding an eye-watering 103 from nine overs - the worst ever ODI figures by an England bowler.

Jacks said of Curran: "I've been through operations and it's always a bit tense playing your first few games and keeping your fingers crossed that your body holds up and you get into the game.

"They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in for any bowler and he bowls a lot of pressure overs - that's his role in the team. He's been so successful with that for England over a number of years.

"There are some days where it doesn't quite work. If they're going to chase 430 then someone's going to have to get some tap, but it's more of a bowling unit problem that we lost that game."

While the bowling came under scrutiny, Jacks believes they found the "perfect batting template", with his close friend Brook recording the all-time fastest ODI double-hundred and the first by an England batter.

Image: The records broken by Harry Brook during his stunning ODI double hundred for England

Jacks, who was at the other end when Brook reached the milestone, added: "From when I went in, he was on 90, so to see him get to a hundred and then a double hundred - which we didn't even really think about until the last two overs - was amazing.

"He's someone I've played a lot of cricket with and to be at the other end and have the best seat was really special, I loved it."

Sports.title: Newey responds to Horner's 'abandon ship' criticism
Sports.content:
Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.

Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024.

But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014.

Red Bull initially continued to be powered by Renault, as in their four title-winning years under the previous rules era, but the French manufacturer struggled with the new regulations, which compromised the performance of the team's Newey-designed car.

Writing in his newly-released autobiography, Drive, Horner recounted a period mid-way through 2014 when he became disappointed in Newey after the legendary designer had received an offer to join Ferrari and was mulling whether to leave.

Horner wrote: "I stood behind him and believed that he stood behind me as well. But at the first sign of adversity, Adrian wanted to abandon ship. I felt very sad about that."

Horner added that, despite Newey's importance to the team, "I could no longer rely on him. Our partnership was not as solid as I had previously believed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner explains how he convinced Niki Lauda to sign Hamilton for Mercedes in 2012.

Horner's comments were put forward to Newey in Friday's team principals' press conference at the United States Grand Prix.

"You're quite right in saying that, no, I haven't read any of it [the book] yet," replied Newey.

"I think 2014, as a chassis designer, if the PU [Power Unit] manufacturer has a bad year, that happens and you accept it.

"If the PU manufacturer has a bad year and doesn't appear to have any intention of trying to address the problem, that's altogether a different matter and that's quite bleak at that point. And that's the situation that unfortunately we faced in 2014.

Image: Adrian Newey and Christian Horner on the Red Bull pit wall in 2014

"And as it turned out, that situation didn't really change with that supplier until we changed to Honda in 2019.

"So, you can imagine my pain and frustration at that. I don't think Christian fully understood that, perhaps. But I was in conversation."

Ultimately turning down Ferrari's offer in 2014, Newey signed a new contract to stay at Red Bull but began to split his time with other projects at the company outside of F1.

Newey stayed a further decade at Red Bull before leaving eventually in 2024 to join Aston Martin the following year, where he is team principal and managing technical partner.

Newey added: "The rest of it [in the book] I really can't comment, but Christian and I remain friends. As many of you know, I am godfather to his daughter Olivia, so, yeah."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner explains the reasons behind why he left Red Bull Racing.

In interviews publicising his book, Horner said he saw similarities between Newey's current experience of trying to turn around a struggling Aston Martin team to their early years at Red Bull following the energy drink's buyout of an underachieving Jaguar outfit in 2005.

It was a comparison that Newey agreed with.

"I think there are actually a lot of parallels between when I started at Red Bull and when I've started at Aston Martin," said Newey.

"Both teams that through their history had had quite a lot of turmoil with changes of owners, changes of senior managers, etcetera.

"It's then really trying to, as we've spoken before, get everybody working together, try to break down silos, improve the culture. And that's been exactly the same again."

Speaking to Sky Sports News earlier this week, Horner said: "Adrian is without doubt the best designer that Formula 1 has ever seen. His track record speaks for itself.

"Lawrence [Stroll] is a very successful guy. He's a very driven guy and has obviously invested heavily in that team. Honestly, I think they've got their own journey that they're on, and it'll be interesting to see how it plays out."

Sports.title: 'A clear red' - Should Ipswich's Diop have been sent off?
Sports.content:
Issa Diop escaped what Oliver Glasner called "a clear red card" during Ipswich's 1-1 draw with Nottingham Forest - but the incident split opinion, so was it the right call or not?

With less than five minutes of the second half played when Diop slid in on Forest's James McAtee, a sending off could have transformed the outcome of the game.

Glasner was adamant Diop had denied a clear goal-scoring opportunity. But Diop himself told Sky Sports he was "quite confident" he would stay on the field as the officials and VAR came to their decision.

There was also split opinion among the Sky Sports pundits, too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oliver Glasner and Gary O'Neil's post-match reaction to Issa Diop's controversial foul on James McAtee.

On co-commentary, Lee Hendrie reckoned Diop was "really lucky" and criticised the reasoning from the referee. Post-match, Ashley Young defended the decision.

Here we break down the key moment - and ask you to have your say.

What happened?

Ipswich centre-back Diop slid in on McAtee, missing the ball and making contact with the Forest player as he tried to break through on goal.

Ref Thomas Bramall didn't blow his whistle but was then advised by VAR to go to the pitchside monitor to review the incident "for a possible denial of an obvious goal-scoring opportunity".

Image: The considerations when officials are making a decision on whether a player has denied a clear goalscoring opportunity

After watching replays, ref Bramall announced it was a foul and then said: "However, because the player knocks it to the right side of the goal, the final decision is direct free-kick and a yellow card to No.6."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ashley Young and Steve Cooper discuss whether or not Issa Diop denied James McAtee a clear goalscoring opportunity.

McAtee's touch

In his announcement, Bramall indicates that McAtee's touch before he is fouled by Diop means the situation cannot be deemed as an "obvious goal-scoring opportunity".

It's a subjective call.

McAtee touches the ball forwards. That takes the ball into the box and slightly to the right.

Significantly to the right? "I do not think he has touched it away from goal at all," said Hendrie on Sky Sports commentary.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the Premier League match between Ipswich Town and Nottingham Forest.

Glasner later argued that moving the ball to the right would have increased the possibility for McAtee to score.

"When you run against the keeper and you run straight, often the angle is not really good, so we are telling the players to sometimes create an angle and I think he prepared his finish by going a little bit half-right, so the keeper has to move and opens the near or far post."

Image: The explanation released by the Premier League Match Centre on the Diop-McAtee incident

More to the ref's reasoning?

But it seems there were other factors on Bramall's mind, too.

Soon after the incident, the Premier League Match Centre posted an explanation on social media of what had happened, including both the on-field announcement from Bramall but also a sentence he said during the decision-making process.

"It's a heavy touch, with the defender inside and he knocks the ball away from the goal - I'm going to go direct free-kick and yellow card".

Bramall didn't mention the "heavy touch" in his announcement at Portman Road - but was McAtee ever actually going to reach the ball after he knocked it forwards? Leif Davis was the Ipswich defender "inside" the ref is referring to.

"McAtee isn't going to get there before Davis. He's quick," said Ashley Young on Sky Sports. "Plus, the ball is going through to the goalkeeper. I think the goalkeeper is going to get there as well.

Diop also used Davis' presence in his defence. "I did the tackle because I saw Leif coming and covering and also he pushed the ball wide and too far."

A decision to debate!

"The red card will split decision," said former Forest boss Steve Cooper afterwards on Sky Sports.

"Forest fans and staff and players will feel hard done by but if it had gone against Ipswich, they would definitely have felt hard done by."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Gibbs-White feels the decision not to give Issa Diop a red card for fouling James McAtee was probably the right decision, but was frustrated it had to go to VAR.

There was even division on whether it was right for Bramall to wait for VAR to intervene, with Gibbs-White and Cooper critical of the ref for not making the decision initially, while Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil praised the process.

A controversial way to kick off the Premier League weekend. Have your say on the incident in our poll above!

Sports.title: Dubois on the lesson of Fury-AJ: 'I want to fight Itauma sooner'
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois believes he and Moses Itauma must learn a lesson from Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua – if they are to fight, they need to do it sooner rather than later.

Fury and Joshua have been British heavyweight rivals for almost a decade but missed the chance to fight each other at the peak of their careers, though they will now finally box in December.

A major rivalry for the next generation of British heavyweight boxers could develop between Dubois and Moses Itauma.

Dubois is a two-time world champion and still only 29 years old. Itauma is just 21 and already a world title challenger.

Dubois thinks Itauma will return to world title contention. "Of course he can. He had the whole industry behind him. They won't let him give up I don't think," Dubois told Sky Sports.

"It was a great fight between him and Hrgovic, so there's no shame in that really. Hgrovic just showed him that there's always someone out there that's stronger willed than you. More determination and he's got kids to feed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the WBO heavyweight rematch between Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley. Video courtesy of DAZN

Dubois can see Itauma becoming a future opponent for him. "Let's see what happens," the WBO champion said. "I'm the one experienced in these situations now. So let's see."

For him there is a lesson to draw from the Fury-AJ example - don't wait too long.

"I want to fight him [Itauma] sooner," Dubois said. "Moses, anyone that can give me a challenge. All the toughest fighters out there I want to face.

"Let's see. I'll break them down now. I feel like I'm at that stage now. I know how I'll have to break them all down, whoever I get in the ring with next, I'll smash them up."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Toe2Toe, Delicious Orie, Barry Jones and Sam Noakes reflect on Moses Itauma's defeat to Filip Hrgovic.

Dubois showed his full wrecking force when he defended his WBO title in just two rounds in his rematch with Fabio Wardley. He's convinced he is the hardest puncher in world boxing.

"I am. I've shown myself over the years as well," he said. But he promises there's still more to come.

"I don't think I've even touched the surface yet really. I'm just starting to unload properly now. It's going to be a good few next fights," he smiled with an innocent menace.

The setbacks he's had earlier in his career, the stoppage loss to Joe Joyce, being bamboozled and beaten twice by Oleksandr Usyk, he reckons have shaped him into the fighter he is today, a fighter, that is, who is arguably the most dangerous heavyweight in the world today.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the IBF heavyweight world title fight between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic. Video courtesy of DAZN

"Who's had a career like mine? Coming back from losses and then banging out good fighters. So I've been showing myself that I've got that power for a long time," Dubois said.

"Broken me down and rebuilt me again a few times. It's interesting.

"Of course, from the first fight with Joe Joyce, a few, Usyk and all those events I feel like they make you stronger."

His fearsome confidence was on display as he ruthlessly bombarded Wardley into submission. But Dubois described it as something else.

"I'd say call it determination, just call it determination, will to win and a little bit crazy," he said.

He laughed deeply. "So it's good."

Sports.title: Leclerc warns Ferrari to ‘be careful’ after setting early US GP pace
Sports.content:
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc edged out Kimi Antonelli to complete a Friday practice double at the United States Grand Prix.

After narrowly topping Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the opening session, Leclerc improved by almost eight tenths of a second later in the day to finish 0.042s clear of Mercedes' Antonelli, who could become Formula 1's youngest ever world champion on Sunday.

Verstappen appears to be in contention to extend his streak of two successive victories after finishing the second session in third, within a couple of tenths of Leclerc's leading time of 1:35.291s.

Lewis Hamilton was unable to match his team-mate Leclerc's pace all day, and had to settle for fourth as he finished more than six tenths back from the Monegasque.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell was given a black and white flag for forcing Charles Leclerc off track during second practice at the United States Grand Prix.

George Russell was fifth in the other Mercedes, but will also be looking for overnight answers as he finished seven tenths back from his team-mate.

Antonelli could clinch his maiden title if he wins on Sunday, and Russell and Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.

The 20-year-old Italian had to overcome some early disruption as his seat became loose, which left him needing to pit and leave the car for the best part of 10 minutes as the issue was repaired.

McLaren suffered a disappointing day as Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri finished seventh and eighth, with both failing to deliver clean laps on their soft-tyre runs.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen made this cheeky move on Liam Lawson as he came out of the pit lane and nips around the outside on the RB first corner.

Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull have each brought upgrades to the event, while Mercedes are still trying to optimise the package they brought two rounds ago in Malaysia that has so far failed to deliver the improvement they anticipated.

Antonelli said: "It was a bit of a difficult start because the seat was not fixed properly, so it kind of felt a bit like being on a rollercoaster on lap one, with the seat moving in the high speed.

"We lost a little bit of time, but it was still a good recovery. I felt better in the car compared to FP1. There's still lots of work to do but it was a good step forward, and now we'll try to improve even further for tomorrow."

Ferrari's package, which featured updates to the car's floor, sidepod and diffuser, appeared to offer hope the Italian team could end a run of eight races without victory, but Leclerc preached caution after his strong day.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ted Kravitz talks through Ferrari's fourth and final upgrades for the United States Grand Prix.

"The feeling is quite good, but we need to be careful," Leclerc said. "It's only Friday and we are seeing what we expected but, again, it's definitely not what everybody thinks in terms of upgrade and lap time gain.

"But it has been a good day. The balance of the car was good and straight away we started in a good window. That paid off and obviously all the hard work that has been done in order to bring this upgrade as soon as possible is also helping us a little bit.

"But we shouldn't carry too high expectations going into tomorrow because I feel like the others have more potential to unlock for sure. Kimi and Max seem to be very, very strong, The McLaren I don't really know yet, I don't think they put everything together yet. But Kimi and Max will definitely be up there."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Friday practice at the United States Grand Prix, a cautious Charles Leclerc shares his thoughts on Ferrari's upgrades.

There was early drama in the session as Russell was investigated for forcing Leclerc off track, but the stewards decided that there had been "nothing dangerous" in the manoeuvre as no further action was taken.

Verstappen's team-mate Isack Hadjar cut a frustrated figure over team radio as he could only manage ninth, with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson taking advantage to claim an impressive sixth.

Williams suffered a torrid afternoon as Carlos Sainz was 20th and team-mate Alex Albon 22nd as their car struggled to meet the challenges of the high-speed circuit.

Sports.title: Littler begins quest for clean sweep in style as No 1 dominates in Dortmund
Sports.content:
Luke Littler began his quest of completing the clean sweep of major honours with an opening win over Willie O'Connor at the Machineseeker European Championship on Friday night in Germany.

Littler is in Dortmund, trying to win the only big event he has yet to claim in a dominant first two years on the scene.

He got off to a good start on Friday night with a 6-3 win over O'Connor, with six 180s to set up a second-round clash with Nathan Aspinall.

European Championship: Night Two Results

Round One

Jermaine Wattimena 6-3 Ryan Joyce Krzysztof Ratajski 6-2 Dave Chisnall Nathan Aspinall 6-3 Cristo Reyes Jonny Clayton 6-3 Niko Springer Luke Littler 6-3 William O'Connor Martin Schindler 6-5 Wessel Nijman Kevin Doets 6-3 Michael van Gerwen Josh Rock 6-1 Chris Dobey

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Matt Edgar discusses why Luke Littler played in the World Youth Championships and whether he will compete in the remaining ProTour events

The teenager is set to take part in a huge Netflix show next week where 24 players are vying to win £501,000 by beating him in a one-off leg, and asked whether his focus is on this tournament, he said: "This is the next one after the World Youths, so I knew how much time I would have off.

"Obviously, (I've played) a few exhibitions, but yeah, just obviously been chilling out, practicing, and this is the one I really want."

The 19-year-old has not played since a surprise defeat in the World Youth Championship and has enjoyed the break.

"I think I'm more focused because of the amount of time we've had off," he added. "I mean, I have not been doing too much, but I've been practising.

"I've just got to take it one game at a time, and obviously it's the last one missing, so I can't be putting too much pressure on myself.

"I'm just happy to get back on stage and do my job."

Littler also revealed he had changed his grip and throw during a lengthy recent lay-off from competitive action to stave off a feeling of boredom in practice.

"I think it's just having so much time off. I had loads of weeks to prepare for this, so I can just go to the practice board at home and just kind of change it, really," he said.

"I hit a nine-darter the other night on DartCounter as well, so I was like... 'I think I will stay with this until something does go wrong'. But it is all going well so far."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn thinks Littler is a natural born darts player and that the 19-year-old needs to show people boos won't put him off his game

Van Gerwen crashes out

Image: Four-time winner Michael van Gerwen was dispatched by Kevin Doets

After Luke Humphries withdrew with illness, Littler's possible path to glory looks even easier as Michael van Gerwen crashed out on Friday night.

Van Gerwen is not the player of old and went out 6-3 to Dutch compatriot Kevin Doets.

"It was a tough game," assessed Doets, who will take on Krzysztof Ratajski on Saturday evening.

"The draw comes out and I get Michael… it's still Michael van Gerwen. He is the one I looked up to for years and the most successful player from the Netherlands.

"He didn't play like he can, but I'm really happy to win. I felt through the whole game that I was the better player.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Nicholson questions whether Michael van Gerwen will ever find his best form again...

Ryan Joyce also had a day to forget as he suffered a 6-3 defeat to Jermaine Wattimena.

Joyce travelled from the North East on Friday morning, but his luggage did not make it to Dortmund.

He had to borrow some darts from a local collector, who had a similar set to the one he uses.

But he found himself 5-0 down and faced darts for a whitewash before putting up a brief fightback.

Aspinall set up his tie with Littler after reeling off four straight legs to see off Cristo Reyes, including finishes of 134, 112 and 90 to come back from behind.

There were also wins for Josh Rock and Martin Schindler.

The European Championship continues with a crucial double session on Saturday, as all 16 remaining players return for round two.

Defending champion Gian van Veen takes on Luke Woodhouse in the pick of the afternoon ties, while Littler and Aspinall lock horns in the evening session.

Sports.title: Wade equals try-scoring record in Newcastle win over Sale
Sports.content:
Christian Wade equalled Chris Ashton's top-flight try-scoring record as he inspired Newcastle to their first Gallagher Prem win of the season over Sale.

Wade matched Ashton's 101 tries when he sprinted over in the 49th minute as Red Bulls recovered from a 3-0 interval deficit to blow Sale away 17-3 at Kingston Park.

Newcastle captain George McGuigan grabbed the other home try, with Josh Hodge adding seven points from his boot.

Ben played an hour in his first league start of the programme, having sat out almost all of last term with hamstring trouble, while Tom made just his fourth appearance for club and country since February, making it through to 10 minutes from time.

The contest was a far cry from the fireworks the two teams produced back in May when the host club fought back from 35-10 down to snatch a thriller at the death 45-42.

The win looked unlikely when Bath exercised total domination for most of the first half, but somehow Gloucester survived for a morale-boosting victory.

For Bath, it was a disappointing night as they fell to their third consecutive defeat and lost both Santi Carreras and Guy Pepper to injuries.

Freddie Thomas and Max Llewellyn scored Gloucester's tries, with George Barton converting both and adding three penalties, whereas a try from Kepueli Tuipulotu was Bath's sole response.

Gloucester had the better of the early exchanges before Bath suffered a huge blow when former Gloucester favourite Carreras slipped and damaged an ankle. The full-back received lengthy treatment on the floor before being helped off to be replaced by Ciaran O'Donoghue.

Bath overcame this setback to produce their first attacks of the night. They too turned down two kicks at goal and looked to have taken the lead when Tuipulotu was awarded a try, but TMO replays showed that the hooker had been hauled down short of the line as he tore away from a driving line-out.

Bath were still able to maintain the pressure by besieging the opposition line. Gloucester conceded a number of penalties and eventually their wing Ollie Thorley was yellow-carded for persistent team infringements.

Another try was awarded, this time to Bath's Enoch Opoku-Gyamfi, but again the try was score was ruled out as the lock lost possession before touching down.

Gloucester conceded 11 penalties in the first 27 minutes and it came as no surprise when prop Ciaran Knight became their second player to enter the sin-bin.

Remarkably it was Gloucester who scored the first points after 31 minutes, when Barton knocked over a penalty after Pepper was adjudged to be off-side.

Gloucester were back up to 14 when Barton soon kicked two penalties in quick succession, but with the last move of the half Bath scored at long last with a try from Tuipulotu from a driving line-out to leave them trailing 9-5 at the interval.

After the restart, Will Joseph became the third Gloucester to be yellow-carded as the centre deliberately knocked on but once again Bath butchered their opportunities and they were made to pay.

Gloucester broke out to secure an attacking platform with Caolan Englefield and Jack Clement making key contributions for Thomas to force his way over.

Bath suffered another blow when their international flanker Guy Pepper was helped off, forcing wing Louie Hennessey to pack down in the back row at the next scrum and their miserable night was complete when Llewellyn forced his way over.

Sports.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
Sports.content:
Take captaincy from Fernandes, then try to sell him and Martínez

The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor.

Ensure the players connect with the fans

Seven hundred United supporters made the trip to Lombardy and witnessed a horror show in incessant rain as their team folded against Cesc Fàbregas’s side. Yet, as always, the faithful will be there on Sunday desperate to cheer their men on against Bournemouth and beyond. Carrick constantly talks of how fans are the club’s lifeblood but do all of the players feel this? Performances such as that at Como will surely be averted if a base creed citing how fundamental supporters are to United is laid down to the squad by the manager.

Play with joy again

Sir Alex Ferguson’s flying wingers, Sir Matt Busby’s holy trinity of Best, Law, Charlton, the “attack, attack, attack” mentality: none of this is evident currently on the field; part of what Carrick admitted on Friday had been “lost”. What is needed is a return to this tradition, and this team are capable as was evident in the spirit of Carrick’s first game of his second tenure. Then, on 17 January 2026 at Old Trafford, he sent out an XI that went at Manchester City from the opening whistle, gave Pep Guardiola’s men zero time to breathe, and a rousing 2-0 victory sent all of a United stripe home jubilant. This, basically, was Carrick’s side last season, a proposition that played with a bounce that landed in third place. This term the smile has vanished and a prevailing sense of doom has settled over the club – precisely what Carrick had vanquished after the gloom of Ruben Amorim’s final days. Time to restore the cavalier edge.

United have suffered, in part, this term owing to Carrick’s drive to move to a more possession-based proposition. The problem is one of the key midfielders recruited to execute this, Youri Tielemans, does not have the legs for a central role, and so has been fielded at 10, while Kobbie Mainoo, who can run an engine room, is injured, and Fernandes’ penchant for running about, out of position, means gaps appear where a ball receiver should be.

Give the young players more of a chance

In Fernandes, Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot, Marcus Rashford, Amad Diallo and Martínez there is a core of long-serving senior players who are not performing. To wake this cadre and freshen the mood from what feels a pervasive staleness, why not blood, more regularly, the younger players? The “play the kids instead” trope can be a cliche but it is a truism for a reason: youth has zero to lose, should run around with a smile and can brighten the darkest of times. Shea Lacey, a nippy wide man, Harry Amass, a promising left-back, and the Fletcher twins, Jack, a clever No 10, and Tyler, a defensive midfielder, are 19 and have 22 appearances between them. None could do worse than those senior players ahead of them.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Get the attack firing

In seven of their 11 games this season United have scored either a solitary goal or none, a shocking statistic that shows up how dysfunctional the attack is and, as part of the creative collective, the midfield too. United have only 10 goals in seven league outings and in three Champions League games have managed five – four of these against the minnows Sabah. At Como there was, again, zero pattern of play, control and a paucity of chances that has to be a serious concern. This has to change or a relegation fight could be United’s. A more off-the-cuff style, allied to an attacking outlook, would suit Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and others and start menacing teams again as United did when beating City, Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool last year.

Sports.title: Enciso rescues point in storm for Ipswich to deny Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Amid a Suffolk squall, winds whipping, a constant drum of rain, an encounter full of half-chances, mistakes, the obligatory refereeing controversy and searching questions. Do Ipswich possess the stones to deal with the big league? Perhaps so. How long can Nottingham Forest’s dip sustain before their president, Evangelos Marinakis, takes his usual course of action. Perhaps not much longer.

Ipswich’s Gary O’Neil was the happier manager, Forest had created the cleaner opportunities, only for familiar failings to cost them. “We were never quite good enough with the ball to turn it into a football match,” said O’Neil. Further adding to Forest’s disappointment, Ipswich’s Issa Diop escaped what looked, on first glance, a red card for a last-man foul. A first-half exchange of goals, both owing much to defensive laxness, determined the result.

Ipswich’s aim is to establish themselves as Forest have in the Premier League. Though Forest and their manager cannot be presumptive of their statuses. “The result doesn’t reflect the performance but I don’t see another solution other than to keep going,” said Oliver Glasner. Forest have six points from eight matches, just a single win.

Glasner admitted he is still “waiting for this click” while saying: “I see great togetherness. The spirit I start to feel … I loved everything I saw today, just not the result.” A record of starting slow only to flourish at previous clubs offers partial protection, though Forest’s ownership is not like other clubs’. Wednesday was the anniversary of Sean Dyche’s appointment. That tenure lasted just 100 days.

Liam Delap’s presence in the Forest ranks, the striker barracked at every touch by home fans, served as a reminder of Ipswich’s failed mission two seasons ago. Unloved in Ipswich for decamping to Chelsea, Delap continues to be short of the confidence he showed back then.

Forest kicked off as lowest scorers in the division; no side had drawn a blank more often. Their drought did not take long to break but no flood followed. Neco Williams’s goal came via an overlap and then a looping cross from Daniel Muñoz. Williams glided in unmarked, his finish low and true beyond Christian Walton.

Another Forest goal appeared likely before home fans, previously exasperated, were lifted by Jaden Philogene forcing a save from Matz Sels and Julio Enciso dancing through red shirts to force another.

The equaliser came via a collective loss of concentration characteristic of Forest’s season so far, echoing defeat at Crystal Palace, and at home to Coventry. Jair Cunha gallivanted forward and, adrenaline coursing, lost possession. Dara O’Shea’s punted clearance was poorly dealt with by Nikola Milenkovic, an under-amped back-pass allowed Enciso to show admirable calm when others had surrendered theirs.

Forest’s failure to claim the rewards on offer from the first half told a familiar story. So too do repeated refereeing controversies, and howls of conspiracy among their supporters. How the officials, led by Thomas Bramall, the referee, did not view Diop’s clattering of James McAtee as a foul defied belief. Play was waved on. More understandable, if still highly debatable, was the verdict via video assistant that McAtee had conceded possession with a heavy touch as the collision came. “Leif [Davis] was there to cover,” said Diop, shown a yellow card. “I don’t think it’s a red.”

“I think they came to the right conclusion, a good process,” O’Neil said. As well he might. “It looks like the VAR was not from the East Midlands today,” said Glasner. “It felt like it was a red card.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Injustice fuelled Forest though did not make them any more clinical, the best of their second-half flurry of chances involved Murillo missing a free header from a corner. That asked for staying power from Ipswich. So far this season, they have not been the soft touch under O’Neil they became in Kieran McKenna’s survival attempt. “We had to show another side to get something,” said O’Neil. “We can play better but if we think we’re going to be dominant in every game … we’ll be fighting for scraps a lot of the time.”

Luck was definitely ridden. Callum Hudson-Odoi, as eight messy minutes of injury time were being added, received more than enough time and space to do far better than drag beyond the far post. The story of the night encapsulated for Forest. And of their season.

Sports.title: Premier League news: Spurs’ nine injuries ‘normal’, says De Zerbi; ‘emotional control’ keeps Blues red-free
Sports.content:
1. ‘Big confidence’ in Tottenham’s injury team Roberto De Zerbi has insisted Tottenham’s medical staff bears no responsibility for the numerous selection issues he faces against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday where his club will attempt to win for only the second time in 42 matches in all competitions. The head coach has been boosted by the return of Pedro Porro from injury while he reported that Andy Robertson, Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke were “good” in light of fitness concerns. De Zerbi had bad news elsewhere, however, saying Destiny Udogie was still out and Tosin Adarabioyo was a doubt. James Maddison did not train for three days after the home win over Coventry on Monday and may not be ready, while caution will remain the watchword with Dejan Kulusevski, who played his first minutes since May 2025 against Frank Lampard’s side. De Zerbi could be without nine players due to injury when the longer-term absentees are factored in, including Lucas Bergvall and Savio. Rodrigo Bentancur is suspended. Spurs appointed a new performance director last season in Dan Lewindon and he oversaw a clutch of new hires in the performance department in July. De Zerbi made the point that the club would make a “total report” on injuries at the end of the season but “so far we can’t say anything bad about the medical staff”. “I am convinced our medical staff this season is high level. I have big confidence because I know how they are working and they are good enough to believe in. We are suffering a normal situation in football.” De Zerbi went into detail on the cases of Porro, Bergvall and Robertson to reinforce his argument. “Pedro won the World Cup with Spain,” he said. “Maybe with the head or body he didn’t recover enough to start this season without a pre-season. He already suffered in the World Cup the muscular problem of the hamstring. He felt it in training and played anyway against Aston Villa [on 29 September] because he pushed to come back before the right time and he suffered another injury. What is the responsibility of the medical staff? “Bergvall turned his knee and felt pain in the first minute against Manchester United [on 10 October]. He finished the game and the day after he felt pain. What is the responsibility of the medical staff? Nothing. Robertson played four games in a row for Scotland [during the recent international window] and after that felt a small problem and did not play in Manchester. He played 65 minutes against Coventry and was fatigued. It’s normal fatigue for a player who played [so much].” On Spurs’s terrible record at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi said: “What is the problem? We didn’t play in the past for Tottenham and I was not the Tottenham coach in the last seasons. We have already many problems and this is not a problem.” David Hytner

2. Alonso: ‘We keep calm, don’t lose our heads’ Xabi Alonso has said greater emotional control is behind the improvement of Chelsea’s disciplinary record, one that saw them picked up 11 red cards last season. Alonso focused on the problem after becoming manager last summer and has been rewarded with better behaviour from his new side. Chelsea, who can expect a feisty encounter when hosting Tottenham on Saturday evening, have not had a red card this season and showed intelligence when they won 2-0 at Everton last weekend. “For me it comes a lot with emotional control, with the control of the game,” Alonso said. “If you are focused on what you have to do, you are prepared for what’s going on. Normally you don’t make that many mistakes and don’t overreact to certain situations. “This is a fundamental part of the game, to have that emotional control. The momentum is coming – we keep calm, I don’t lose my head and I don’t get stupid yellow cards, make stupid penalties.” Alonso pointed to Chelsea signing more experienced players last summer. “I think it helps,” he said. “Absolutely. It helps for that composure that you need in certain moments. You have players that sometimes, even during the game, they take a step back to see this is happening and now we need to keep focused and calm.” Stamford Bridge is usually at its loudest when Spurs turn up at a ground where they have not won since 2018. Alonso expects an “electric” atmosphere but admitted that playing with control in the Premier League can be tough when crowds feed off duels and end-to-end football. “It is really difficult,” he said. View image in fullscreen Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has played down the impact of his influence from the touchline: ‘I have from the touchline some kind of input but the real one is from the players.’ Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters “To find a total dominance in a game when you are in full control and you have few problems like in other leagues, it’s difficult to find it in the Premier League unless you have become a top, top, top team. That’s why you can’t rest on your laurels when you are 2-0 up.” Alonso played down the impact of his influence from the touchline. “It is people on the pitch,” the Spaniard said. “I can say many things but sometimes I don’t reach [the players], I don’t control. I can do it in advance. I have from the touchline some kind of input but the real one is from the players. Normally the most experienced ones. It’s the ones that feel it.” Chelsea are without Emiliano Martínez after the goalkeeper broke his jaw against Everton. Mike Penders will start and Alonso sees similarities between the young Belgian and his compatriot Thibaut Courtois. “I spoke with Thibaut as well when he was in the World Cup, asking about Mike, and he even said that he could see resemblances with Mike,” Alonso said. Jacob Steinberg

3. Go easy on Ngumoha, says Iraola Andoni Iraola has insisted Rio Ngumoha must be allowed to make mistakes and not have his development stifled by “impossible” demands. The 18-year-old sparkled for Liverpool in their Champions League comeback against Villarreal on Tuesday while still adapting to playing on the right wing. It was only a fifth start under Iraola for Ngumoha, who last month became the third-youngest player to make his competitive debut for England, after Wayne Rooney and Jude Bellingham. The Liverpool head coach has described it is a “privilege” to coach the teenager but is wary of too many expectations being heaped on such a young talent. “I feel very lucky to have him but this is a moment when, because he has played well, we cannot straight away put expectations on him super high because it is not fair for him,” Iraola said. “He will still have to make mistakes, he will still have his moments where it is up and down, because this is a natural process that every player goes through. “We cannot straight away put demands on Rio that are impossible to beat. No, we have to help him in this process knowing that he will have good games and probably some games when it is not so good.” Iraola believes Ngumoha’s personality offers reassurance that he will not be unduly affected by the growing attention. The winger has two years remaining on the contract he signed on turning 17 but is expected to be rewarded with a new deal. “I haven’t felt that he’s very affected, positively or negatively, by all the things that are said about him,” Iraola added. “He’s very focused on the football side, on improving his performances and trying to get the things that we need from him. It’s not easy when you are 18 and everyone is talking about you but he knows that what matters is what is happening today in training and the things that he can add to his game. He’s very focused on that.” Liverpool will again be without the injured Dominik Szoboszlai when hosting in-form Brighton on Sunday and Victor Muñoz is doubtful with a knock sustained in last weekend’s win at Brentford. Andy Hunter View image in fullscreen The 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha sparkled for Liverpool in their Champions League comeback against Villarreal on Tuesday. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

4. Farke faces triple injury blow Daniel Farke has been dealt a blow before Sunday’s Premier League game at Sunderland after revealing Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Anton Stach and Noah Okafor are all injury doubts. Calvert-Lewin, whose fourth league goal of the season earned Leeds a 1-1 home draw against Manchester United last week, and midfielder Stach both sustained foot injuries in that match. Winger Okafor is struggling with a thigh strain and all three players are rated “major doubts” after missing out on team training this week. Farke confirmed Daniel James is in restraint after recovering from his recent injury, while Lukas Nmecha, Harry Wilson and Jean-Mattéo Bahoya will also be hoping to feature. Nmecha has made six league appearances off the bench this season and Farke added: “Overall you have to say for a back-up striker, Lukas has scored I think seven goals last season,” said Farke. “Of course, if he doesn’t play each and every minute due to the fact that Dominic was so outstanding, I think this is a really good record and I would have to say in the last game he looked sharp.” Press Association

5. Nothing has changed for us, says Arbeloa Alvaro Arbeloa maintains “nothing has changed” as his Fulham side look to build on a first Premier League win. The Spaniard – who took over as head coach at Craven Cottage in the summer – has come under scrutiny following a testing start to the campaign before easing some of the pressure with a 1-0 victory over Hull at Craven Cottage. Fulham come up against another promoted side at Coventry on Saturday and Arbeloa wants his players to continue to show the same focused mindset. “Nothing has changed for us,” Arbeloa said. “When we were not winning games, we believed that we were doing so many things well, and now we have the same targets, so we should come in and try to win a tough game. “Yes, now we have the reward that we were looking for, and now it is another week, another game, so we need to fight again for the win.” Arbeloa added: “When you are working and you are not winning, it is not easy, so everything is easier when you play well, in the way that you want and you win matches. That is the most important thing, and it is very important for your confidence, and I think we deserve it.” Press Association

Sports.title: Arteta concerned over Saka’s durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue.

Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Saka missed a large portion of last season due to hamstring, hip and achilles tendon injuries having also been sidelined by another hamstring issue in 2024-25. In total, he has had 11 different injuries since September 2023 and Arteta insisted that he has been trying to ease his workload as a result. “It’s certainly been different in the last year or so,” the Spaniard said when asked if Saka remains robust enough to start every match. “The demands that we are putting on every player are immense. The amount of games, the intensity of those matches, the international competitions, the times as well between games are getting narrower.

“Bukayo against Lille [in the Champions League last week] didn’t start the game because we knew what was happening. We have to play three times in less than six days. And especially when the games are so demanding, until the last minute you are there, you are chasing the game, you want to win. The necessity is to win every game, so we know that. So we are preparing the players for those scenarios and we do the best that we possibly can.”

Saka missed only three Premier League matches in three seasons between 2021 and 2024 and broke the Arsenal club record by playing in 83 consecutive top-flight games. He is already approaching 300 appearances for the club he joined as a seven-year-old and was rewarded with a lucrative new contract in February that made him one of the highest-paid players in the club’s history.

Asked whether he feared Saka could suffer from burnout having made his Arsenal debut three months after his 17th birthday, Arteta said: “I don’t have that feeling at all but something we have to be very mindful of is to create the right ecosystem around the player to fulfil his qualities. We really need to understand, whenever he comes back, how we are going to manage his load, what he is capable of to sustain having an impact in the team.”

Saka had only three weeks off after the World Cup but Arteta rejected suggestions that he should have been given more We want to pick on something, we will find it, but we won’t know whether it is for that or not. Maybe we needed to load those tendons more during those three weeks? Because if you don’t load the tendons, it becomes a problem. Who knows? I don’t know.”

Saka’s absence could hand an opportunity to Max Dowman on Saturday. The 16-year-old has played only nine minutes in the league this season and Arteta feels sure he is ready to make an impact after he became the youngest goalscorer in Premier League history, against David Moyes’s side in March.

“There is something inevitable to go back to that memory and the feeling of the moment. That’s with us, that’s going to stay in that stadium for a long, long time,” said Arteta. “He’s training and every time he’s got a moment to play, he’s showing that he’s a player that is going to impact the game. For sure he’s going to have minutes.”

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany taken to hospital after collapsing at Bayern training
Sports.content:
Vincent Kompany has been ⁠taken ⁠to ​hospital after the Bayern Munich coach felt unwell during training ⁠on Friday.

The Belgian, ​who ‌had been ‌nursing a virus in ‌recent days, was coaching his team before feeling unwell and being taken to ‌hospital.

The Bundesliga leaders, who drew 2-2 ​at home against Arsenal in the Champions League on Wednesday, are due ​to ​travel to ​Freiburg on Sunday. Kompany was on the bench for the Arsenal game despite the viral infection.

Bayern said on their website: “Vincent Kompany required medical ⁠attention after collapsing during a training session for ​Bayern’s reserve team. The ‌head coach of the professional squad had been observing ‌the second team’s session.

“Kompany is currently undergoing a thorough examination in the hospital and will remain under medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage all training ‌and match-related operations.“

Max Eberl, Bayern’s sporting director, said: “Vincent Kompany’s health is our top priority. At Bayern, we will do everything ​we ​can to ensure he ​makes a speedy recovery.

“Vinnie is receiving ​all the ‌necessary medical care ​and ​support, and he will be given as much time as he needs. Everyone at FC Bayern wishes Vinnie a quick recovery.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace and Newcastle face off with both in search of season kickstart
Sports.content:
Are the team underperforming?

Conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League matches is not exactly the start Pierre Sage or Crystal Palace’s hierarchy would have hoped for. The transition from Oliver Glasner’s counterattacking 3-4-2-1 formation to the Frenchman’s more aggressive approach has exposed massive weaknesses in defence, culminating with last week’s humiliating defeat at Brighton. Palace fans became used to success under Glasner and they are already looking nervously over their shoulders at the bottom three. Even their league wins under Sage so far – against Fulham and Nottingham Forest – could have ended in defeat. Something doesn’t seem right in south London. EA

There have been so many arrivals and departures on Tyneside in recent months that it’s too early to say. Any team that sold their three best players – Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimarães in Newcastle’s case – during the summer would expect a degree of disruption. Eight signings were made, with four aged 20 and under and the others aged 24 and under, and only one (Nico González) had Premier League experience. Throw in a change of manager and an almost entirely new backroom staff and playing style three weeks before the season and teething troubles seem almost inevitable. LT

How much pressure is the manager under?

Sage is sailing extremely close to the wind and was warned after the Brighton game that things must improve quickly or he will be shown the door. It is understood that the Palace chair, Steve Parish, has yet to be convinced by the manager who led Lens to the French Cup last season and has demanded improvements in defence. After the creditable Europa League draw with Besiktas in midweek, Sunday’s meeting with Newcastle is crucial to his future. Thomas Frank and Kieran McKenna are likely candidates should Sage get sacked. Ipswich would be due substantial compensation for McKenna despite him leaving Portman Road in the summer, which could be a major hurdle. EA

View image in fullscreen Adam Wharton (centre) looks dejected during Crystal Palace’s defeat at Brighton. Photograph: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

Very little internally but, externally, the honeymoon is over. Newcastle paid Saudi Arabia’s Al-Ahli £9.5m compensation for Matthias Jaissle, convinced that the 38-year-old German and his “vertical football” were ideal fits. David Hopkinson, the chief executive, and Ross Wilson, the sporting director, are very impressed by Jaissle’s management style, particularly his collaborative approach. They appreciate that Eddie Howe’s successor is new to the Premier League, did not have a proper pre-season and is coping with a raft of injuries. All parties remain sufficiently realistic to predict a season of “ups and downs” but Newcastle’s Saudi Arabian owners crave a return to Europe. Many fans believe Jaissle’s football is old-school, rudimentary long ball with a fancy name, and believe his system and team selections have been flawed. They fear he may be a slave to philosophy. LT

How much responsibility does the manager bear?

Palace have looked a shadow of the side that won three trophies in the space of 12 months under Glasner and Sage must take some of the blame. He fell out with Parish after failing to sign several of his preferred targets in the summer, but it was his decision to break up the Adam Wharton-Daichi Kamada axis in central midfield having brought in Quinten Timber on deadline day. While the Dutchman, who missed the game in Turkey due to injury, has provided extra energy and Kamada has excelled in a more advanced role, Wharton has been struggling defensively. Palace looked much more solid when Wharton and Kamada started together against Besiktas – surely Sage will now stick with the partnership that served Glasner so well. EA

Jaissle’s belief in a gung-ho 4-2-3-1 featuring a classic No 10 is serving him badly at Newcastle, where he does not possess a natural attacking playmaker. It is also leaving González, a holding midfielder, frequently overrun and in need of additional support. With Malick Thiaw and, particularly, Sven Botman struggling in central defence, a switch to a more stable 3-5-2 may be sensible. More importantly, changing the philosophy to a more contain-and-counterattack approach would help camouflage the flaws and make the most of the team’s blistering attacking pace. Jaissle’s high-pressing, attack-minded tactics often appear overly high-risk. His critics fear he may prove to be another Ruben Amorim but Newcastle insiders insist Howe’s successor will prove more flexible than he may seem. Newcastle have not kept a league clean sheet for 13 games, equalling a club record, but six of those came under Howe. LT

How much is beyond the manager’s control?

A typically chaotic end to the transfer window left Sage with a bloated squad but insufficient leadership at the back after selling Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea. Axel Disasi’s three-match ban due to a reckless red card against Ipswich, after he arrived on loan from Stamford Bridge along with the promising Italian teenager Honest Ahanor, hasn’t helped. Parish and the sporting director, Matt Hobbs, deserve criticism for not bringing in more experienced replacements, with the latter’s position also thought to be under heavy scrutiny. Sage has also had to deal with unhappy attackers in Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, who made no secret of their desire to leave Selhurst Park in the summer. EA

Quite a lot. Given his late arrival, Jaissle had limited influence over Wilson’s eight summer signings. He has, though, apparently swiftly decided that Aladji Bamba (£34m from Monaco) and Bazoumana Touré (£43m from Hoffenheim) are not ready to be thrown into Premier League combat. Similarly, the fleet-footed £51m former Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo looks as if he is going to need time to adjust. Newcastle’s policy of generally recruiting players under 25 dictates the dressing room is a little light on leadership. Meanwhile iIt is hard to say whether the manager’s high-intensity training bears any responsibility for a lengthy injury list, with Anthony Elanga, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey notable absentees. LT

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Matias Fernandez-Pardo, seen here rounding Coventry keeper Carl Rushworth but failing to score, will need time to adjust to the Premier League. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

How important is winning this game?

After seeing positive signs against Besiktas, as Mateta scored on his first start since the opening day, three points on Sunday will be crucial for Sage. Yet while Palace haven’t lost to Newcastle at home since November 2020, Jaissle’s side have had extra time to prepare and will present a difficult challenge. EA

Given that Newcastle are 11th it is far from imperative. And yet after a demoralising 4-1 defeat at Coventry and a 1-0 home reverse against Aston Villa, victory would offer much-needed reassurance regarding the team’s potential and boost player confidence, not to mention quieten the social-media noise surrounding Jaissle and his tactics. LT

Are there any reasons for optimism?

Palace’s summer net spend of almost £40m in profit was the second lowest in the Premier League behind Aston Villa. They also have American owners who are estimated to be worth a combined £10bn. But Parish revealed last month that he is still looking for extra funding for the new main stand at Selhurst Park, with Woody Johnson, Josh Harris and David Blitzer thought to be open to selling their shares after Palace enlisted Raine Group to seek fresh investment in the club. So there is plenty riding on making sure there is no prospect of being relegated. Sage showed at Lens that he is capable of building a winning team and needs time to do that. EA

Yes, quite a few. Jaissle, understandably, does not want to overplay the 18-year-old central midfielder Sean Steur but the summer signing from Ajax is a joy to watch, has a wonderful passing range and looks capable of reaching the top. Lewis Hall, the England left-back, looks to be going from strength to strength and is capable of elevating standards. Despite an undoubted dogmatic streak, Jaissle appears intelligent – and humble – enough to learn from his mistakes and make necessary adjustments. Club insiders cite his refreshing willingness to listen. Newcastle also possess several extremely quick attacking players – and, as coaches rarely tire of pointing out: “If you’ve got pace, you’ve got a chance.” LT

Sports.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start
Sports.content:
Most footballers like to spend their summers unwinding after a long season but not Pascal Gross. Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024, the midfielder entered – and won – a running race.

Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor.

Gross was moving from Brighton to Borussia Dortmund after seven years in the Premier League and reported to his boyhood club for pre-season training days later. Running is an obsession for Gross, as it is for his former teammate James Milner, who revealed last month he was training for a marathon after finally hanging up his boots, and that has shown since he returned for a second spell at the Amex in January for a bargain £1.2m.

“I think he’s looking in his free time now: ‘Where can I run a race?’ Because he will never stand still,” joked Brighton’s head coach, Fabian Hürzeler, after the 35-year-old scored the opening goal in a 3-0 victory over Arsenal last month. “ During the off-season he’s never the person who can lay on the beach for several hours and do nothing. He always needs to do something.”

Given that Gross has this season racked up an average distance of more than 11.5km per match and has covered the third-most ground of any player in the Premier League, it is no surprise Hürzeler has compared his compatriot to a good wine: “The older the wine gets, the better it gets.”

That analysis is borne out by the rest of his statistics this season as Brighton have emerged as challengers for Champions League qualification, at the very least, before Sunday’s game at Liverpool. Not only has Gross, the Premier League’s player of the month for September, contributed a combined seven goals and assists, he is in the top five for several other metrics such as big chances created (six), chances created from open play (14) and line-breaking passes leading to a goal (three). In a team that have scored the fourth-most goals (23) in Premier League history after seven games, Gross has been the standout performer.

View image in fullscreen Pascal Gross (in white) up against Jablonec's Matej Polidar in the Conference League. The match finished 0-0. Photograph: David W Cerny/Reuters

“Sometimes he’s just one step ahead than his opponent,” said Hürzeler, who is understood to have been instrumental in bringing back Gross. “He might not be the quickest player, but he can be the quickest in the head and sometimes being the quickest in the head is very helpful. No one expected that it would be this good. But it also shows that he still has this capacity in his body.”

At a club where experience is valued despite Hürzeler being the youngest permanent manager in the Premier League’s history, insiders describe Gross as the perfect role model for some of Brighton’s younger players. Charalampos Kostoulas has scored three goals in his past four league matches and the 19-year-old Greece striker is clearly thriving alongside the man who is approaching 300 appearances for the club. Diego Gómez, the dynamic Paraguayan who scored a goal-of-the-season contender against Crystal Palace that will go down in Brighton folklore, the homegrown talent Jack Hinshelwood and the midfield linchpin Yasin Ayari are others benefiting from his vast experience, as is Hürzeler.

Gross managed 75 Brighton goals and assists after joining from Ingolstadt in 2017 in the summer when Brighton were promoted. His departure for Dortmund, a year after his first Germany cap, was to fulfil a boyhood dream but there was always something drawing Gross – who wears a long-sleeve shirt owing to a grass allergy – back to the club where he is known as the Kaiser.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“It was really difficult,” Gross said of his Brighton exit. “Only something really special got me out of here. There were a couple of other options [before returning], but Brighton was always the priority. I just stayed in touch with all the lads over the time away. Maybe you watch less of the games or you don’t stay in touch as much any more, it gets less and less. But it never really did.”

Gross retiring from international football after the World Cup has also been to Brighton’s benefit. His status as a club legend was augmented by delivering the free-kick that Palace’s Jaydee Canvot headed into his own net during the 5-0 humiliation on Sunday. That was the third game in a row in which Gross has provided an assist and he has an opportunity to become the oldest player to make it four since Chelsea’s Gianfranco Zola in December 2002.

The trip to Anfield continues a gruelling run of five away fixtures in a row. Brighton drew at the Czech club Jablonec on Thursday in the Conference League and after Sunday they go to Manchester City twice in four days – the first in the Carabao Cup – before heading to Spain to play Getafe. It will test Brighton’s mettle after their spectacular start. Hürzeler can count on Gross – who has started every game in all competitions – to last the course.

Sports.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
Sports.content:
It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 goals in two games are not the side whose head coach is under most pressure before a north London derby.
