World.title: US House Odds Favour Democrats at 91%
World.content:
The Rayburn House Office Building on Capitol Hill, home to Representative Pramila Jayapal’s Washington office (Photo: ajay_suresh, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Traders now put the chance of Democrats winning the US House at about 91%, according to the two biggest prediction markets, with 10 days to the 2026 US midterm elections on Tuesday, 3 November. The Senate is far closer, at about 67%.

Key Facts Prediction markets, House: Democrats 91.5% on Polymarket and 91% on Kalshi, as of 11:50 p.m. ET, 23 October.

Prediction markets, Senate: Democrats 67.5% on Polymarket and 67% on Kalshi, same time.

Latest poll: New York Times/Siena, 21 October: Democrats lead the House ballot 52% to 41% among likely voters.

Senate math: Republicans hold 53 of 100 seats, so Democrats need a net gain of four.

Election Day: Tuesday, 3 November 2026; each state sets its own polling hours.

This story is part of our coverage of the 2026 US midterm elections. Dates, times and how to follow it are in our guide. Latest: Canada Denies US Claim of Midterm Meddling

What Prediction Markets Say

At 11:50 p.m. ET on 23 October, Polymarket priced a Democratic House at 91.5% (about US$21.1 million traded) and Kalshi at 91%. For the Senate, Polymarket showed Democrats at 67.5% (about US$8.8 million traded) and Kalshi at 67%.

Polymarket’s “Democrats Sweep” contract, which pays if Democrats win both chambers, stood at 66.5%, down 2 points in 24 hours. Republicans keeping the Senate while losing the House stood at 24.5%.

These prices are real-money bets, not polls, and they can move within minutes. Kalshi is regulated in the US by the CFTC, the federal derivatives regulator.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on US Midterms 2026 Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the Senate Is Harder

Republicans hold 53 of the 100 Senate seats, while Democrats and two independents who vote with them hold 47. A 50-50 split would be broken by the Republican vice president in the Republicans’ favour.

Democrats therefore need a net gain of four seats for a majority. The Cook Political Report, a nonpartisan forecaster, projects a Democratic gain of two to six Senate seats, a range that leaves control open.

Voters wait in line for early voting in Metairie, Louisiana, in October 2024 (file photo; Photo: Infrogmation, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Polls and Close Races

The New York Times/Siena College poll, released on 21 October, found Democratic House candidates ahead 52% to 41% among likely voters. It also put President Donald Trump’s approval at 36%, with 59% disapproving, the lowest in any Times/Siena poll.

In the same poll, 69% disapproved of Trump’s handling of the cost of living and 65% of the Iran war. Harvard’s Institute of Politics, in a survey released on 22 October, found Democrats ahead 63% to 26% among 18-to-29-year-olds who say they will definitely vote.

In Colorado’s 3rd District, a Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee poll of 402 likely voters on 20-21 October had Democrat Dwayne Romero at 47% and Republican Jeff Hurd at 46%, within its 4.9-point margin of error. In South Carolina’s 1st District, a poll sponsored by the Democratic group House Majority PAC on 21-22 October had Democrat Nancy Lacore at 47% and Republican Jenny Costa Honeycutt at 45%, while Polymarket priced Honeycutt at about 60%.

What to Watch

About 23 million ballots had been cast by 23 October, according to the TPS Elections early-vote tracker. That total does not show who is winning, because the party split of early voters is not a result.

The Federal Reserve’s next rate decision is due on Wednesday, 28 October, at 2:00 p.m. ET (18:00 UTC), six days before Election Day. Our guides explain when polls close and how the midterm odds work.

What It Means for US Readers

The markets treat the House as close to settled, while control of the Senate is still open. That gap matters for anyone following judicial confirmations, the federal budget or trade policy, because the Senate handles all three.

Prices are a snapshot and can shift with each new poll or early-vote report. A reader who wants the wider picture can start with our explainer on the 2026 midterms.

What Is Not Known

Whether the Democratic lead will turn into the seats needed for Senate control is not known. Late-deciding voters, turnout and remaining early voting could narrow or widen it.

Sponsor-funded district polls may not reflect the final electorate, and market prices may change before 3 November. Ballot totals and race results stay unknown until votes are counted and certified.

Sources

Polymarket (House, Senate) and Kalshi, read at 11:50 p.m. ET on 23 October 2026; New York Times/Siena College poll, 21 October; Harvard Kennedy School Institute of Politics; Colorado Public Radio; Cook Political Report; TPS Elections.

World.title: Latin American Pulse for Saturday, October 24, 2026
World.content:
Brazil votes Sunday in a runoff that polls call a technical tie, while Argentine bank shares jump about 5% in New York and Chile's peso slips.

Rio Times · Latin America

Key Facts —Brazil Anxious but hopeful as polls call the runoff a technical tie before Sunday’s vote. —Mexico Steady stocks and a firmer peso, while diesel gets no tax relief for a sixth week. —Argentina Cautiously optimistic as bank shares jump about 5% in New York. —Colombia Peso gains 0.3% as oil rises about 3%. —Chile Quiet and slightly softer: stocks slip 0.3% and the peso loses 0.9%. —Prediction markets Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 79% and Kalshi at 78% (Lula: 21% and 23%), as of 24 October, 2:00 am ET; prices are bets, not polls.

Source: market close, 23 October 2026.

The Continent’s Mood Today

The region spent Friday waiting for Sunday’s presidential runoff in Brazil. Markets elsewhere moved in small steps, and only Argentina’s bank shares made a big jump.

Currencies told a mixed story: the Brazilian real gained 1.6% against the US dollar, while Chile’s peso lost about 0.9%.

Brazil – A Runoff Too Close to Call

Brazil votes on Sunday 25 October in a presidential runoff between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. An Alfa Inteligência poll released on 23 October, with fieldwork from 18 to 22 October, put Flávio at 49.9% of total votes and Lula at 46%.

That equals 52% to 48% of valid votes, a technical tie inside the poll’s 1.9-point margin of error. Traders on Polymarket and Kalshi, who bet real money, see it differently and give Flávio about a 78% chance of winning.

The last television debate of the campaign was due on Globo on Friday evening. Flávio has said he would treat the PCC and Comando Vermelho gangs as narcoterrorist groups, while Lula stresses federal coordination on security.

Brazil’s central bank approved rules on 23 October that make lenders offer a clear way to block credit advertising and a single dashboard of a customer’s debts. The rules take effect between March and July 2027.

The Ibovespa, Brazil’s main stock index, rose 0.47% to 205,083, and the real strengthened to 4.97 per US dollar. Mid-month inflation for October was 0.32%, down from 0.70% in the previous reading.

For a foreigner holding Brazilian assets, Sunday is a test of political stability. Polls and prediction markets differ on who is ahead, so Monday’s trading could be volatile.

Mexico – Fuel Costs and a Steady Market

Mexico’s IPC stock index slipped 0.30% to 69,678 on Friday, while the peso gained 0.3% to 18.65 per US dollar. For the week of 17 to 23 October, the finance ministry cut the share of the gasoline tax it waives for regular Magna petrol to about 59% from 64%.

Diesel received no tax relief for a sixth week in a row. For a foreigner living in Mexico, fuel and transport costs are creeping up even as the currency holds steady.

Argentina – A Bank Rally in New York

Argentine shares listed in New York rose sharply on Friday: Banco Galicia gained 5.0%, Banco Macro 4.9%, oil producer Vista 6.0% and YPF 3.1%. We could not confirm Friday’s closing level of Buenos Aires’ own Merval index in time for this report.

Argentine shares have swung sharply in recent weeks, so one strong day is no guarantee of a trend. Foreign investors tend to read the New York listings first because they trade in US dollars.

Colombia – The Peso Gains with Oil

Colombia’s peso gained 0.3% to 3,187 per US dollar on Friday. Oil, the country’s largest export, rose about 3% as Brent crude moved above US$116 a barrel.

For a foreigner with operations in Colombia, higher oil prices help both the currency and government revenue. A reversal in crude would quickly show up in Bogotá’s markets.

Chile – A Softer Peso on a Quiet Day

Chile’s IPSA stock index slipped 0.31% to 10,746 on Friday. The peso weakened 0.9% to 995 per US dollar.

Chile’s economy leans on copper exports and is sensitive to global risk appetite, which fell on Wall Street on Friday. A weaker peso makes imported goods costlier for households.

The Shared Mood

The region’s Friday was shaped by outside forces as much as local ones: a stronger real, a weaker Chilean peso and pricier oil. Brazil’s vote is the immediate test, and the result will set the tone for the region’s markets on Monday.

For a foreigner, the continent offers opportunity but demands a clear view of risk. Sunday’s runoff in Brazil is the first thing to watch.

01 The AI trade loses its shine

The Dow fell 1.23% to 52,215 while the S&P 500 slipped 0.52% to 7,624, as investors questioned whether the enormous funding needs of AI data centres can deliver adequate returns. The Nasdaq’s milder 0.21% decline to 25,955 masked deeper losses in AI-linked names, with Meta down about 7% on Thursday and a further 1% on Friday as investors weighed its heavy spending plans.

Gold fell 0.75% to US$3,994 an ounce even as shares slid, with a firmer dollar and higher yields weighing on it. The VIX jumped 2.21% to 19.45, a sign that caution is creeping back into options markets after a long calm.

02 The Fed faces hot prices, cooler nerves

The US 10-year Treasury yield rose about 4 basis points to 5.00%, up from 4.96% on Thursday, as price pressures persisted. October’s composite PMI of 57.6 showed output-price growth at its strongest since August 2022, even as new orders grew at their fastest pace in about four and a half years.

Michigan consumer sentiment held at 48.0 against 48.1 a month earlier, while one-year inflation expectations held at 4.7%. That combination argues against an easy policy pivot at next Wednesday’s Federal Reserve meeting, where markets broadly expect rates to stay on hold.

03 Brazil’s election and the dollar test

Brazil enters its presidential runoff on Sunday with markets already on edge from global forces. October’s IPCA mid-month inflation came in at 0.32% month on month, slowing sharply from 0.70% in the previous reading.

World.title: Trump Floats Ships Off Cuba, Havana Rejects
World.content:
El Capitolio, Havana's former seat of government, and classic cars. File photo, 2025. (Photo: fragandaphoto, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Key Facts Who: President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Cuban leaders in Havana.

What: Trump floated a US ship stopping about 50 yards off Cuba’s coast; Havana rejected the threat.

When: Friday, 23 October 2026, at a Republican rally in Fort Myers, Florida.

Next: The UN General Assembly holds its annual vote on the US embargo later this month.

Prediction markets: Kalshi prices a US–Cuba trade deal before 2027 at 16% (10:22 p.m. ET, 23 October).

This story is part of our coverage of the Cuba US tensions. Who backs Havana, the blackouts, the embargo vote and what it means for travellers are in our dossier. Latest: Second US Aid Flight Lands in Matanzas, Cuba

President Donald Trump said on Friday that US ships returning from operations against Iran could pass Cuba, with one stopping “about 50 yards off the coast.” Cuban leaders answered the same day, rejecting what they called a threat, in the latest turn of the Cuba news we track.

The remarks came at a Republican rally in Fort Myers, Florida, a state with a large Cuban-American electorate, 11 days before the US midterm elections on 3 November.

Trump Floats Naval Pressure

Trump told the rally the United States would “take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran,” according to NTD and PBS video of the event. He said Cuba would “raise up their hands” and that he would “send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal.”

Havana Rejects the Threat

President Miguel Díaz-Canel wrote on X that Washington “does not renounce its ambitions of domination” over Cuba, in a post quoted by Periódico Cubano. Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez wrote that Cuba rejects every threat and said its coast would be an inhospitable place for anyone arriving with hostile aims.

Both posts appeared on Friday; their exact times were not published.

The Capitolio and the Gran Teatro in central Havana. File photo. Photo: Silva Selva, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Rubio Courts Cubans With a CIA Offer

Rubio posted on X on Friday urging Cubans to seize the moment “through a discrete partnership with the CIA,” as reported by Yahoo News. The agency then published a Spanish-language video with instructions for making contact.

The Pressure Campaign So Far

On 30 January Trump signed an order threatening tariffs on countries that sell oil to Cuba, according to Al Arabiya. In June, Washington sanctioned Cuban entities including the mining firm Geominera and the steelmaker Siderúrgica José Martí, ABC News reported.

On 19 October the two governments clashed at UN headquarters in New York, where US Ambassador Mike Waltz led a panel on Cuban human rights ahead of the annual vote on the US embargo.

Kalshi, an exchange regulated in the US by the CFTC, prices “Will Trump announce a trade deal with Cuba?” at 16% before 1 January 2027, with 69,008 contracts traded as of 10:22 p.m. ET on 23 October. That is a bet on a deal, not a poll and not a forecast of military action.

What It Means for You

For US readers, the remarks show how Cuba policy is entering the closing days of the midterm campaign, where Florida votes carry weight. For travellers and investors, the practical rules still come from sanctions and licences, not from rally speeches.

What Is Not Known

It is unclear whether the ship idea is an operational plan, a negotiating line or campaign rhetoric. The content of the “deal,” any date for a Rubio trip and the exact date of the UN vote were not public.

World.title: Power Failure Disrupts Costa Rica’s Juan Santamaría Airport Control Tower
World.content:
A power failure temporarily knocked out critical air traffic control systems at Costa Rica’s Juan Santamaría International Airport today, raising new concerns about the reliability of equipment at the busiest airport. The electrical problem affected the control tower for nearly an hour, reportedly leaving air traffic controllers without their usual radar screens, communication systems, weather information and radio equipment. During the outage, personnel were left relying on a portable backup radio to communicate with aircraft.

The failure prompted a temporary interruption in airport operations while technicians worked to restore the equipment. However, Costa Rican authorities said the situation was resolved quickly and maintained that scheduled flights were not affected. Public Works and Transport Minister Efraím Zeledón confirmed the electrical failure and said officials initially feared the disruption could last considerably longer. Technical crews were able to restore the affected systems before that became necessary.

Costa Rica’s Civil Aviation Authority also confirmed that normal operations had resumed, including both arrivals and departures. Aeris, the company that operates Juan Santamaría International Airport, said the control tower’s systems were fully restored. Nevertheless, the company advised travelers to contact their airlines directly to confirm their flight status.

The incident raises questions about the reliability of the airport’s electrical infrastructure and whether adequate backup systems are available when critical equipment fails. Air traffic controllers depend on radar, radio communications and weather information to safely coordinate aircraft approaching, landing and departing. When those systems become unavailable, airport authorities may need to restrict operations until normal service can be restored.

Today’s incident is not the first time technical problems have disrupted Costa Rica’s main international airport. On September 12, a truck damaged fiber-optic cables near the airport, temporarily interrupting radar communications, flight-processing systems and airline check-in services. The incident forced some airlines to process passengers manually and resulted in lengthy lines and flight delays.

An even more serious electrical failure occurred last September, when problems with the radar system forced Costa Rica to close its airspace for nearly seven hours. The disruption affected operations at both Juan Santamaría and Guanacaste Airport in Liberia, delaying, diverting or canceling numerous flights.

Following that incident, authorities announced plans to improve the electrical infrastructure supporting the airport’s radar equipment. The latest failure comes as Costa Rica continues to face questions about the reliability of its aviation infrastructure, including technical problems and shortages of air traffic controllers.

Although toay’s outage was relatively brief, it highlighted how quickly a technical failure can affect the systems responsible for managing commercial air traffic. Authorities have not publicly established the precise cause of the latest electrical problem or explained whether it was related to previous infrastructure failures.

For travelers, airport operations have returned to normal. Passengers departing from or arriving at Juan Santamaría are encouraged to check directly with their airlines for the latest flight information.

World.title: Gian Teck begs court for mercy after pleading guilty to having sex with 14-year-old girl; ‘Didn’t know what he was doing’ despite previous case involving other 14-year-old girl
World.content:
Gian Teck begs court for mercy after pleading guilty to having sex with 14-year-old girl; ‘Didn’t know what he was doing’ despite previous case involving other 14-year-old girl

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Twenty-two-year-old Gian Teck, who pleaded guilty to unlawful sexual intercourse with a 14-year-old girl, appeared before Justice Nigel Pilgrim in the High Court on Thursday, October 22, where he pleaded for forgiveness and mercy ahead of his sentencing. Notably, this is Teck’s second offense for sex with a 14-year-old girl involving a minor in a separate incident.

“I just want to ask for forgiveness from the court. I didn’t know what I was doing at the moment. I want the court to consider me and have mercy on me,” Teck said during his mitigation hearing.

Teck was 18 years old when he engaged in sexual intercourse with the minor at his home on June 5, 2023. He initially denied the charge but changed his plea to guilty on October 1, on the fourth day of his trial, after the victim testified behind closed doors.

His attorney, Javier Williams, urged the court to impose a sentence at the lower end of the sentencing range, arguing that Teck was young and immature at the time of the offense and had no previous convictions.

Crown Counsel Kirk Brown, representing the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, argued that Teck should receive only a limited reduction in his sentence because his guilty plea came after the trial had already begun and the victim had been required to testify.

While both sides discussed a sentencing range of two to four years under the applicable sentencing guidelines, Brown maintained that the court should not impose a sentence below the five-year statutory minimum. The offense carries a prison term of five to ten years.

The prosecution also raised concerns about the possibility of Teck reoffending and requested that the court order counselling as part of his rehabilitation.

According to the agreed facts, the minor visited Teck’s home on June 5, 2023, where they engaged in sexual intercourse. During a subsequent police interview, Teck admitted having sexual intercourse with the girl on three occasions but claimed he believed she was 15 years old.

Teck had previously faced separate allegations involving another 14-year-old girl. However, that case was discontinued in January 2026 after the complainant declined to testify. Justice Candace Nanton explained at the time that the prosecution’s decision to enter a nolle prosequi did not amount to an acquittal and that the charges could be brought again.

Justice Pilgrim reserved his sentencing decision to consider the submissions made by both sides. Teck is scheduled to learn his fate on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.
